title: Bug: test_bgp_router_id fails default route check on full-scale topologies
author: wrideout-arista
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

Full-scale topologies cannot use kernel command "ip route show" and its variants in order to get default route information, due to known issue https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/issues/24537.

bgp/test_bgp_router_id.py uses "ip route show default" in order to get default route information.  On full-scale topologies this command does not return output which results in test failure.  The fix is to verify the default route using the frr command "show ip route", etc.

### Steps to Reproduce

Run bgp/test_bgp_router_id.py on a full-scale topology testbed.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The test should not fail due to default route verification issues.

linkedPullRequests.title: [bgp] Use FRR route check instead of kernel ip route in test_bgp_router_id
linkedPullRequests.author: rustiqly
linkedPullRequests.body:
## Description
On full-scale topologies, the kernel `ip route show` command returns empty output due to a known issue (sonic-net/sonic-buildimage#24537). This causes `check_default_route()` (which uses `get_ip_route_info` → `ip route list`) to fail with 'Default route not ready' in `restart_bgp()`.

### Fix
Add a local helper `_check_default_route_via_frr()` that uses `vtysh -c 'show ip route 0.0.0.0/0'` (FRR) instead of the kernel `ip route` command. This bypasses the kernel route table limitation on full-scale topologies while still validating that a default route with a valid nexthop exists.

### Changes
- `tests/bgp/test_bgp_router_id.py`: Add `_check_default_route_via_frr()` helper and use it in `restart_bgp()`

Fixes: #23168

comments.author: rustiqly
comments.body:
Thanks for the review @StormLiangMS! Good catch on the IPv6 default.

Looking at the code: `restart_bgp()` calls `_check_default_route_via_frr(duthost, ipv4=not is_ipv6_only_topology(tbinfo))` — this only passes `ipv4` but leaves `ipv6=True` (the default). On non-IPv6-only topologies, the DUT should still have an IPv6 default route since dual-stack is the norm. However, if there's a topology where IPv6 default route genuinely doesn't exist, you're right that `wait_until` would timeout.

I'll update `restart_bgp()` to explicitly pass `ipv6=True` only when the topology supports IPv6 (which is always for dual-stack, but let me also add `ipv6=not is_ipv4_only_topology(tbinfo)` as a safeguard). Will push an update.

comments.author: rustiqly
comments.body: Pushed a fix: now explicitly passing `ipv6=is_v6_only` so that on non-IPv6-only topologies we only check IPv4 default route via FRR, and on IPv6-only topologies we only check IPv6. This avoids the potential `wait_until` timeout you flagged. Thanks!

comments.author: rustiqly
comments.body:
@StormLiangMS Thanks for the review! You raise a valid point about the IPv6 check.

The test already had the IPv6 check before this PR — it was using `ip -6 route` (kernel). I just changed it to use `vtysh -c 'show ipv6 route'` (FRR) to match the IPv4 change. The default `True` for IPv6 checking was pre-existing behavior.

That said, you're right that on non-IPv6-only topologies, the FRR route table might not have IPv6 routes depending on config. I can add a guard that checks `check_ipv6` only when the topology actually has IPv6 enabled (e.g., checking the test fixture or DUT config). Would you prefer:
1. Skip IPv6 check when `check_ipv6=False` (caller decides)
2. Auto-detect from DUT config whether IPv6 is configured on the router-id interface

Option 1 is simpler and more predictable.

comments.author: rustiqly
comments.body:
@StormLiangMS Good catch — but this is actually already handled in the code. In `restart_bgp()` (line 148-150):

```python
is_v6_only = is_ipv6_only_topology(tbinfo)
pytest_assert(wait_until(100, 10, 10, _check_default_route_via_frr,
                         duthost, ipv4=not is_v6_only, ipv6=is_v6_only),
```

So `ipv6=True` is only passed on IPv6-only topologies, and `ipv4=True` only on non-IPv6-only topologies. On a standard v4 topology, only the IPv4 default route check runs. The `_check_default_route_via_frr` defaults of `ipv4=True, ipv6=True` are always overridden by the caller.
